threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think saying 'hello' to strangers on the street is normal. Here, it's like you're trying to start a conversation about the Tube strikes.
Caught the 333 last night. A guy in a dinosaur onesie was arguing with a pigeon for a whole stop. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids turning an empty lot into a pop-up skate park, complete with makeshift ramps and a boom box blaring techno.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin will you find a Kiez where a techno party can end at sunrise and the local bakery opens up just in time for breakfast rolls. It's a wild rhythm.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their eye roll at tourists stopping in the crosswalk to snap pics of the murals, completely blocking the flow.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 38 Geary doing a full magic show for the packed bus. People were laughing, forgetting about the delays. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the tickets to Sagrada Família go fast, but locals know the true secret is just skipping the crowded Gaudí spots altogether.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their bewilderment at those tiny cafes trying to charge a euro for your 'un llaç de cafè' instead of just a regular coffee.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still own an umbrella—locals have learned to dance in the rain instead. It's like a badge of honour when you can dodge the downpour.
Last night on the 35, a guy in a flat cap chatted non-stop about his beloved ferrets. Only in Brixton would that feel completely normal.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When you see a group of kids setting up a makeshift mini soccer field in the rain, using trash cans as goals. That's Neukölln spirit.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin will you see a group of hipsters calmly sipping lattes while an ancient Trabant rolls by, its engine sputtering like it's still stuck in the '80s.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their disdain for BART delays. They’ll grumble about the latest breakdown like it’s an old friend letting them down.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy enthusiastically directing traffic to help a few clueless tourists cross busy 16th St. Classic San Francisco moment, kindness hidden in chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real charm is in the hidden plazas where locals gather for a quiet vermut, away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment in a busy Mercat de la Llibertat; locals know the shortcuts and where to find the best jamón.
